description: Golden C# Tutor prompts used for manual or semi-automatic output quality validation. The health check validates this file structurally; scripts/test-output-quality.ps1 can also score captured answers from tests/answers/<id>.md.

expectedKeyPoints.label: Explains that many LINQ queries are not executed until enumeration
Warns about repeated enumeration or changed source data

rubric: Starts with the direct mental model before advanced caveats.
Keeps the example small enough for a beginner to run.
Connects the example back to the pitfall.

cases.prompt: $csharp-tutor mode=review focus="OOP, clean code" level=beginner. Review a BankAccount class with public Balance setter, Withdraw allowing negative amounts, and no tests.

expectedKeyPoints.label: Leads with correctness or safety findings
Recommends validation for deposits or withdrawals

rubric: Separates required fixes from optional style tips.
Shows a concrete refactor direction without rewriting unrelated code.

cases.prompt: $csharp-async review this ASP.NET Core service method that calls httpClient.GetStringAsync(url).Result inside a request handler.
rubric: Does not overclaim that every ASP.NET Core .Result call deadlocks.
Explains why the change improves correctness or scalability.

cases.prompt: $csharp-security review an ASP.NET Core endpoint that reads a file using Path.Combine(root, userProvidedFileName).

expectedKeyPoints.label: Recommends canonical path validation or allow-listing
Checks the resolved path stays under the root

rubric: Explains the failure mode without exaggeration.

cases.prompt: $csharp-tutor mode=docs explain records vs classes and cite official Microsoft docs.

expectedKeyPoints.label: Distinguishes reference type classes from record behavior
Mentions generated value equality or nondestructive mutation
Separates language facts from design guidance

rubric: Cites or explicitly calls for official documentation.
Does not flatten records into DTO-only guidance.
Includes a concise example only if it clarifies the rule.

cases.prompt: $csharp-efcore review a query that uses Include to load entities and then maps them to DTOs for a read-only API response.

expectedKeyPoints.label: Mentions tracking behavior for read-only queries
Suggests inspecting generated SQL or measuring

rubric: Explains why projection can reduce loaded data.
Avoids absolute performance claims without evidence.
